author: Nomadcxx
title: fix(shell): stop the lock preview only while one runs (sysc-2418)
text:
Fixes sysc-2418.

While the session is sealed, `coordinateBackground` called `walls.StopPreview()` on every pass. `walls.Service.stopPreview(nil, …)` publishes a snapshot even when no preview is running ("No Preview session is active."), and `relayWalls` → `applyWallsSnapshot` calls `queueBackground()` for every snapshot. So each pass queued the next one, for as long as the session stayed locked.

Measured on archPC while locked (build eabafb28): 157% CPU, 115k read and 18.8k write syscalls a second. A CPU profile's hot frames were exactly the cycle: `autoPauseInputs`, `Config.Clone`, `coordinateBackground`, `syncAutoPause`, `LoadLease`, `relayWalls.func1`, `applyWallsSnapshot`.

The fix stops the preview only when the walls snapshot reports one running. Every preview state change publishes a snapshot, so a preview that starts after the check still gets stopped on the next pass.

Tests:
- `TestSealedBackgroundSettlesWithoutAPreview`: sealed lease, idle walls service whose `StopPreview` answers like the real one. Before the fix it ran about 14,000 coordination passes in 200 ms; after, it settles.
- `TestSealStopsARunningPreview`: a preview running at seal is stopped exactly once. It fails if the stop is removed.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/shell ./internal/walls ./internal/lock`, `go vet ./...` (capped), gofmt: clean. `-race` ran on the new tests and the managed-snapshot tests only; the full race suite was not run on this machine.

Not yet checked live: the archPC session is still locked on the old build. After it's rebuilt, measure CPU while locked. Also check whether the 18.7k writes a second also appear while unlocked; if so, there's a second cause.
